title: Client token leasing and server reconciliation for duplicate-billing elimination
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: At-least-once delivery semantics (retries, timeouts, client restarts) can cause duplicate ingestion events and duplicate billing in edge cases. Current mitigations (opaque replay tokens and reconciliation sweeps) have reduced but not eliminated billing anomalies for high-retry workloads and cross-region failover. We need a robust, low-latency approach that: 1) prevents most duplicates at ingress, 2) allows safe retries from clients and SDKs, 3) bounds server state growth, and 4) provides deterministic reconciliation for the rare duplicate cases.
proposed_solution: Introduce a client-driven dedup token lifecycle with short server-side lease and a compacting commit-log based reconciliation. Key components: (a) SDK issues a DedupToken per logical user request (GUID + client epoch), (b) token is presented at ingest and granted a short lease (e.g., 30s) by the ingest gateway which records a lightweight committed entry, (c) ingest gateway replies with commit confirmation containing server-lease-id and commit-window, (d) clients may retry with the same DedupToken; server will dedupe if within lease/commit-window, and (e) a background compactor moves committed tokens to a compacted store and emits any necessary billing adjustments. This hybrid model minimizes hot server-side state while keeping duplicate probability negligible for normal retry patterns.
design_tradeoffs_and_notes:
- Lease window length: shorter leases reduce state but increase false-negative duplicates when client-network flaps; we settled on 30-60s initial window with per-customer tuning in later phases.
- Token format: use 128-bit random + client monotonic counter to avoid reliance on client clocks.
- Leases vs. global nonce: leases avoid need for globally-coordinated nonce store at ingest hotspot nodes.
- State growth: compactor sweeps and TTL-based eviction; compactor will run per-customer and emit aggregated metrics for billing reconciliation.
- Quotas interaction: token grant counts towards soft quota reservations to prevent rush storms causing accidental duplicate billing from retry storms.
- Rollout complexity: requires SDK updates, gateway changes, and a short-lived dual-mode (compat + token) period.
acceptance_criteria: SDK can generate and attach DedupToken for each request using new SDK flag (enabled=false by default)
Ingest gateway stores token commitment and returns commit confirmation in <20ms p95 for typical path
Duplicate billing rate reduced to <0.02% on synthetic 10% retry workload while preserving successful throughput
Compactor runs and reduces ingest gateway working set by >95% within configured TTL
Fallback compatibility: clients without DedupToken still accepted and billed under legacy path
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Spike + benchmark in staging using runtime-1.24 feature branch (internal only)
Phase 1: SDK alpha release -> internal apps opt-in; observe duplicate_rate and token store growth for 48h
Phase 2: Gateways default to accept tokens but keep legacy dedupe enabled; invite 5 beta customers
Phase 3: Enforce token-based dedupe for high-volume customers and add per-customer tuning controls in Console
Phase 4: Global rollout and deprecation of legacy opaque-replay-path after 90 days of healthy metrics
metrics: billing.duplicate_rate: percent of ingested requests later flagged as duplicate
ingest.token_latency_p95_ms: latency added by token grant/commit handshake
ingest.token_store_size_per_customer: active tokens in gateway store
sdk.retry_behavior_ratio: percent of retries reusing same DedupToken
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for token lifecycle (issue, attach, commit, dedupe, compaction).
- Load tests with synthetic retry storms (1M req/min) to validate token-store behavior and p95 latencies.
- Chaos tests: gateway process restarts and network partition to validate no double-commit surfaces.
- Billing e2e: create synthetic customers with known generated duplicates to verify reconciliation adjusts billing ledger and notifies customer success when adjustments > threshold.
monitoring_and_alerts:
- Alert if ingest.token_store_size_per_customer > X for 30m.
- Alert on billing.adjustment_count > 0.1% of volume for 1h.
- Dashboard for token lifecycle showing grant rate, dedupe hit rate, lease expirations, and compactor throughput.
security_considerations:
- Tokens are unpredictable and treated as scoped nonces; do not leak tokens in public logs.
- All token persistence uses envelope encryption with customer KMS where applicable.
- Security review required for token format and retention policy to avoid sensitive user data being embedded in tokens.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Raman: Initial triage. Duplicate billing incidents correlated with region failovers and aggressive client retries. Decided to explore client-driven tokens with short server leases.

2026-03-04 - Miguel Soto: Spike complete. Prototype gateway shows p95 token commit latency = 12ms and memory increase ~0.8MB per 100k active tokens. Identified compactor strategy to avoid unbounded growth.
2026-03-07 - Priya Menon (Billing): Reviewed prototype metrics; requested explicit reconciliation event emission to tie adjustments to ledger entries and customer notifications.
2026-03-09 - Security review kickoff (Eleanor): Raised concerns about telemetry containing tokens. Decided to redact tokens in logs and only publish token hashes for troubleshooting.
2026-03-11 - Miguel Soto: Opened PR for runtime gateway changes. Integration tests failing intermittently under very high retry bursts; investigating backpressure tuning and soft quota reservations.
2026-03-12 - Lina Chen (SDK): Draft SDK changes ready in branch; will default off and add opt-in flag. Need to coordinate release window with gateway alpha.
2026-03-12 - Aisha Raman: Updated acceptance criteria to include fallback compatibility and performance target. Planning rollout gating metrics and grace period for legacy path deprecation.
